newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA, techs down amid jitters.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA, techs down amid jitters.

text.p: CompUSA Inc and some technology stocks fell sharply on Tuesday amid increasing concern about the retail computer sales outlook and growing jitters about next week's U.S. Presidential election.
CompUSA and other computer retailers came under pressure after Salomon Brothers issued a report noting a distinct softening in retail computer sales over the last few weeks.
A number of technology shares also succumbed to profit taking as investors, concerned about a possible sweep by the Democrats of both houses of Congress, moved to lock in their gains, traders said.
CompUSA fell 4-5/8, or about eight percent, to 52-3/4. CDW Computer Centers Inc, a direct marketer of personal computers, fell three, or about four percent, to 64.

Other technology shares moving lower included Compaq Computer Corp, down 2-1/8 to 68-1/2, Dell Computer Corp, down 2-5/8 to 78-3/8, International Business Machines Corp, down 1/2 to 126-5/8, and Hewlett-Packard Co, down 3/4 to 44-1/2.
"A number of groups, especially the tech stocks, have been under a bit of profit-taking," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock and Co.

"I think people are worried about the post-election market," Ackerman said. "There is concern that a Democratic control of both houses of Congress may be seen as a catalyst for a market selloff," he said.
"By and large, people are taking profits where they can," he said.
Contributing to the sense of nervousness was a report from Salomon Brothers analyst David Childe that said there has been a distinct softening in retail computer sales over the last few weeks.
Childe, in his report, said CompUSA's retail computer sales, which comprise 60 percent of its business, have decelerated and said the industry's promotional activity is intensifying.
